name: Internet, Memes & Web History
description: Questions covering: Early Web Browsers, Search Engines, Social Networks, Video Sharing...

questions.question: Which early web browser was the first widely popular graphical browser?
questions.explanation_correct: Mosaic was the first widely popular graphical web browser and helped bring the web to mainstream users. It was developed at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are web browsers or browser-related tools from different eras, but they were not the first widely popular graphical browser.

questions.question: Which search engine is the one whose name became a verb?
questions.explanation_correct: Google became so dominant that its name entered everyday language as a verb meaning to search online. It is one of the most recognizable internet brands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are well-known search engines, but their names did not become the standard verb for online searching.

questions.question: Which college-origin social platform was launched by Mark Zuckerberg?
questions.explanation_correct: Facebook began as a social networking site for Harvard students and was launched by Mark Zuckerberg and his classmates. It later expanded to a global audience.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are online platforms, but they were not the college-origin social network launched by Zuckerberg.

questions.question: Which video-sharing website used the slogan 'Broadcast Yourself'?
questions.explanation_correct: YouTube used the slogan 'Broadcast Yourself' in its early branding. It became the dominant platform for uploading and watching online videos.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are video platforms or streaming services, but they were not identified by that slogan.

questions.question: Which platform was formerly known for posts called tweets?
questions.explanation_correct: Twitter popularized short public posts called tweets. It became a major microblogging platform before later rebranding.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are social platforms, but they were not the service historically associated with tweets.

questions.question: Which collaboratively edited encyclopedia was co-founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger?
questions.explanation_correct: Wikipedia launched in 2001 with Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger as co-founders.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Britannica and Encarta were commercial encyclopedias; Wiktionary is a collaborative dictionary.

questions.question: AOL's popular instant messaging software, active from 1997 to 2017, was better known by what acronym?
questions.explanation_correct: It stands for AOL Instant Messenger and was a staple of early 2000s internet culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: ICQ was a separate service acquired by AOL, and MSN belonged to Microsoft.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly abbreviated as IRC?
questions.explanation_correct: IRC stands for Internet Relay Chat, a text-based real-time communication protocol. It has been used for group chat on the internet since the late 1980s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are plausible-sounding expansions, but they are not what IRC stands for.

questions.question: What was the name of the 2007 viral video featuring a feline named Fatso 'performing' on a musical instrument?
questions.explanation_correct: The footage was actually filmed in 1984 but became a massive meme decades later.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nyan Cat is an animation, and the others feature different animals.

questions.question: The meme featuring a cartoon dog sitting in a burning room saying 'This is fine' originates from which comic series?
questions.explanation_correct: The 'This is fine' comic was created by KC Green for his webcomic Gunshow.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other webcomics are popular but did not originate this specific meme.

questions.question: Originating on 4chan, which crudely drawn black-and-white face is the original 'FFFFFFF-UUUUUUUUUUU' character?
questions.explanation_correct: This character kicked off the 'Rage Comics' genre of web humor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Trollface represents mischief, while Forever Alone depicts extreme loneliness.

questions.question: Whose 1987 music video for 'Never Gonna Give You Up' became the core of a famous internet bait-and-switch?
questions.explanation_correct: The 'Rickroll' involves tricking someone into clicking a link that leads to this video.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other singers are British icons but are not part of this specific prank meme.

questions.question: Who created the webcomic xkcd?
questions.explanation_correct: Randall Munroe created xkcd, a webcomic known for stick figures and topics including science and technology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other creators are associated with different webcomics.

questions.question: Which imageboard is closely associated with many early anonymous memes?
questions.explanation_correct: 4chan is the imageboard widely linked to the spread of many early anonymous internet memes. Its anonymous posting culture shaped meme development.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other sites are internet communities, but they are not the imageboard most associated with early anonymous meme culture. They played different roles online.

questions.question: Which system translates domain names into IP addresses?
questions.explanation_correct: DNS, the Domain Name System, resolves human-readable domain names into IP addresses. It is essential for locating servers on the internet.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are internet protocols, not name-resolution systems. They do not perform domain-to-IP translation.

questions.question: Which programmer worked with Eric Bina on the early web browser NCSA Mosaic?
questions.explanation_correct: Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina were key developers of Mosaic at NCSA.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures were not the Mosaic developer described.

questions.question: Who is credited as the inventor of the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation_correct: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN. He developed the core technologies that enabled web pages and hyperlinks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are famous computer scientists or search engine founders, but they did not invent the Web. Their contributions were in different areas.

questions.question: What is the name of Reddit's alien mascot?
questions.explanation_correct: Snoo is the name of Reddit's alien mascot. It appears throughout Reddit branding and community references.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are mascots or characters from unrelated brands. They are not associated with Reddit.

questions.question: Which phrase from the poorly translated opening of the game Zero Wing became an internet meme?
questions.explanation_correct: “All your base are belong to us” comes from a localized version of Zero Wing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phrases come from different games or internet memes.

questions.question: Which 1996 CGI animation of an infant is widely considered one of the very first internet viral sensations?
questions.explanation_correct: It was created as a sample for 3D character animation software and spread via email chains.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are descriptors but not the official name of the file or meme.

questions.question: Which entrepreneur is most associated with founding the blogging platform Blogger?
questions.explanation_correct: Evan Williams co-founded Blogger, which became one of the earliest major blogging platforms. He later co-founded Twitter as well.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are tech founders associated with different companies or products, not Blogger's founding.

questions.question: Which music-sharing service was launched in 1999 by Shawn Fanning and Sean Parker?
questions.explanation_correct: Napster became famous for sharing music using peer-to-peer transfers and a centralized file index.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kazaa, LimeWire and eMule were other file-sharing applications.

questions.question: Who was the performer behind the viral internet video featuring the song "Numa Numa"?
questions.explanation_correct: Gary Brolsma appeared in the original "Numa Numa" video, which became a widely shared early viral clip. His webcam performance helped define early internet video culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are internet personalities or creators, but they were not the performer in the original "Numa Numa" video.

questions.question: Which web comic creator is known for the comic xkcd?
questions.explanation_correct: Randall Munroe created xkcd, a widely read web comic known for humor about science, technology, and relationships. He previously worked at NASA.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are web comic creators or cartoonists, but they did not create xkcd.

questions.question: Which forum software project uses the name phpBB, short for PHP Bulletin Board?
questions.explanation_correct: phpBB is an open-source forum software project written in PHP.
questions.explanation_incorrect: vBulletin, Simple Machines Forum and XenForo are different forum packages.

questions.question: Which cat became the face of the original 'I Can Has Cheezburger' meme?
questions.explanation_correct: Happycat was the subject of the original 'I Can Has Cheezburger' image.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other cats are famous internet figures, but they were not the subject of this specific early meme.

questions.question: Which online encyclopedia project was the predecessor to Wikipedia?
questions.explanation_correct: Nupedia was the expert-reviewed encyclopedia project that preceded Wikipedia. Wikipedia was launched as a faster, collaborative companion project.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are later or different wiki-related projects, not Wikipedia's immediate predecessor.

questions.question: Which search engine was launched in 1995 by Digital Equipment Corporation?
questions.explanation_correct: AltaVista was developed at Digital Equipment Corporation and became a prominent search engine.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lycos, Excite and Dogpile were different search services.

questions.question: What term refers to the stylized internet dialect often used in lolcat captions?
questions.explanation_correct: Lolspeak is the playful dialect associated with lolcat captions, featuring altered grammar and spelling for comedic effect. It became part of meme culture in the mid-2000s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are internet language terms or invented labels, but they are not the lolcat dialect term.

questions.question: Which image format is well known for supporting frame-based animations in a single file on the web?
questions.explanation_correct: GIF supports multiple frames and became a common format for short web animations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: JPEG, BMP and plain text are not the usual animated image format described.

questions.question: Which 1990s browser was released by the company co-founded by Marc Andreessen and Jim Clark?
questions.explanation_correct: Netscape Navigator was released by Netscape, co-founded by Andreessen and Clark.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mosaic was developed at NCSA; Opera and Internet Explorer came from other companies.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages over the internet?
questions.explanation_correct: HTTP is the standard protocol used for requesting and delivering web pages. It underlies how browsers communicate with web servers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are internet protocols, but they are used for file transfer, email sending, or email retrieval rather than web pages.

questions.question: What search engine brand did Microsoft launch in 2009?
questions.explanation_correct: Microsoft launched Bing in 2009.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cortana and Edge serve other roles; MSN is an older Microsoft brand.

questions.question: Which professional networking site is commonly used for resumes and job connections?
questions.explanation_correct: LinkedIn is a professional networking platform focused on careers, resumes, and business connections. It is the best match for the clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are social platforms, but they are not primarily professional networking sites.

questions.question: Which early web portal became famous for its yodeling advertisements?
questions.explanation_correct: Yahoo! was a major early web portal and became well known for its yodeling ad jingle. It was a landmark brand in early internet culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are early web companies or portals, but they are not the one associated with the yodeling ads.

questions.question: Which advice animal meme shows a child in a triumphant pose against a colorful background?
questions.explanation_correct: Success Kid is the meme featuring a child with a clenched fist in a victorious pose, often placed against a bright or rainbow-like background. It became a classic advice animal-style image.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are meme characters, but they do not match the child-victory image described in the clue.

questions.question: A five-second clip from a Japanese variety show features which animal turning around with a zoom-in for comedic effect?
questions.explanation_correct: The animal in the video is actually a prairie dog, despite the popular name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sneezing Panda features a panda cub, and Keyboard Cat is a cat.

questions.question: Who drew the original Trollface in a 2008 webcomic about trolling?
questions.explanation_correct: Carlos Ramirez, known online as Whynne, drew Trollface and posted the comic on DeviantArt in 2008.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are creators associated with different comics.

questions.question: What is the name of the teddy bear associated with the phpBB community?
questions.explanation_correct: Bertie Bear is an icon of phpBB; the first Bertie teddy bear was made available in 2004.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are not the phpBB bear described.

questions.question: What term describes sensational or misleading headlines designed to entice people to click?
questions.explanation_correct: Clickbait uses enticing headlines or descriptions to attract clicks, sometimes by misleading readers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Spam is unsolicited messaging; phishing seeks sensitive information; bait-and-switch is a related but broader deceptive tactic.

questions.question: Which Microsoft encyclopedia was sold on CD-ROM in the 1990s?
questions.explanation_correct: Microsoft Encarta was a multimedia encyclopedia distributed on CD-ROM.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Britannica, Grolier and World Book also published reference works, but Encarta was Microsoft’s product.

questions.question: Which singer performed the wordless song that became known online as the “Trololo” meme?
questions.explanation_correct: Eduard Khil’s televised performance became a viral video commonly called “Trololo.”
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other singers were not the performer in that video.

questions.question: Which late-90s website featured an endless loop of rodents moving to a sped-up version of 'Whistle Stop'?
questions.explanation_correct: Hampton the Hamster later released a full song based on this early web novelty.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are fictional variations of the actual name.

questions.question: What is the term for the internet phenomenon of posting humorous photos of cats with captions in broken English?
questions.explanation_correct: Lolcats are image macros of cats with captions written in a humorous, intentionally broken dialect.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related terms, but not the specific name for the phenomenon or image style.

questions.question: Which protocol name is used for a secure, encrypted version of a web address?
questions.explanation_correct: HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP and uses encryption to protect data in transit. It is the standard protocol indicated by a padlock in browsers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are network protocols, but they do not refer to the encrypted web protocol. They serve different functions or lack the security layer.

questions.question: Which early text-based browser for Unix systems is known for displaying web pages without graphics?
questions.explanation_correct: Lynx is a text-only browser that became known for browsing the web in terminal environments. It has long been associated with Unix and minimal interfaces.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are browsers, but they are not the text-only Unix browser described. They are graphical browsers from different eras.

questions.question: Which search engine was represented by a butler character and later became widely known by that brand name?
questions.explanation_correct: Ask Jeeves was a search engine brand built around the idea of asking questions, with a butler mascot. It later shortened its branding, but the original name is the one asked for.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are real search engines, but they do not match the butler-branded service. They were separate companies with different identities.

questions.question: Which social news site, co-founded by Kevin Rose, let users vote for stories by “digging” them?
questions.explanation_correct: Digg was a social news site where users submitted and voted on links.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Reddit, Slashdot and Hacker News are other social news or discussion sites.

questions.question: Which social networking platform became famous for highly customizable profile pages and an early music scene presence?
questions.explanation_correct: MySpace was a major early social networking platform known for customizable profiles and strong music-community features. It was one of the defining networks of the mid-2000s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are social networking services, but they are not the platform described. They had different launches, audiences, and features.

questions.question: Which video-sharing site was founded in 2004 by Jake Lodwick and Zach Klein?
questions.explanation_correct: Vimeo was founded by Jake Lodwick and Zach Klein and became known for creative video.
questions.explanation_incorrect: YouTube, Dailymotion and Veoh are different video-sharing services.

questions.question: Which early blogging platform was known for user journals and communities and used the domain livejournal.com?
questions.explanation_correct: LiveJournal combined personal journals with community features.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Blogger, Xanga and Tumblr are other blogging platforms.

questions.question: Which proprietary forum package, known for its high-end features, was a top competitor to vBulletin throughout the 2000s?
questions.explanation_correct: Now known as IPS Community Suite, it was a major player in the golden age of forums.
questions.explanation_incorrect: phpBB is open-source, whereas Invision was a leading commercial option.

questions.question: Which meme image shows an unlucky-looking schoolboy associated with constant mishaps?
questions.explanation_correct: Bad Luck Brian is the meme image of a boy whose captions describe embarrassing or unfortunate events. It became a well-known reaction meme online.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Success Kid, Advice Dog, and Scumbag Steve are all meme characters, but they refer to different image memes. The correct answer is Bad Luck Brian.

questions.question: Which internet meme features a flat-faced cat often captioned with an annoyed or displeased expression?
questions.explanation_correct: Grumpy Cat became famous for its distinctive sour expression and was widely used in humorous captions. It is one of the most recognizable animal memes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Keyboard Cat, Lil Bub, and Colonel Meow are all cat-related internet figures, but they are not the specific meme described. The correct answer is Grumpy Cat.

questions.question: Which 2007 home video became a YouTube global phenomenon, featuring a mischievous baby and his older brother Harry?
questions.explanation_correct: It was for a long time the most-viewed non-music video on the platform.
questions.explanation_incorrect: David After Dentist features a child in a car, and the others are produced parodies or rants.

questions.question: Which viral video title is associated with a person enthusiastically lip-syncing to a Romanian pop song in a webcam recording?
questions.explanation_correct: Numa Numa is the widely shared webcam video of Gary Brolsma lip-syncing and dancing to a pop song. It became an early internet viral hit.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chocolate Rain, Guitar Hero Kid, and Evolution of Dance are all viral video titles, but they refer to different clips. The correct answer is Numa Numa.

questions.question: Which reaction image name is used to describe covering one's face in embarrassment or frustration?
questions.explanation_correct: Facepalm refers to the gesture of putting a hand over one's face to show embarrassment, frustration, or disbelief. It became a common internet reaction image and meme.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Shrug, eye roll, and smirk are all reactions, but they describe different expressions and gestures. The correct answer is Facepalm.

questions.question: In which webcomic created by Ryan North do the characters and art stay exactly the same in every single strip?
questions.explanation_correct: Only the dialogue changes, while T-Rex and his friends remain in fixed poses.
questions.explanation_incorrect: xkcd uses stick figures, and the others use varied panel art.

questions.question: Which website became famous as a major online marketplace and auction platform?
questions.explanation_correct: eBay is an online marketplace best known for auctions and person-to-person sales. It played a major role in early e-commerce.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Etsy, Craigslist, and Amazon are all online commerce platforms, but they are not primarily the auction site described. The correct answer is eBay.

questions.question: Which browser shares its name with the Norwegian company that developed it and is known for early tabbed browsing?
questions.explanation_correct: Opera is both a browser and the name of the company behind it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names refer to different browser projects or organizations.

questions.question: Which browser was released by Microsoft and became one of the most widely used in the late 1990s and early 2000s?
questions.explanation_correct: Internet Explorer was Microsoft's flagship web browser and dominated much of the early consumer web era. It was bundled with Windows and became extremely widespread.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also web browsers, but they are not the Microsoft browser described here. Their origins and timelines differ from the correct answer.

questions.question: Which search service is known for emphasizing user privacy and not tracking searches?
questions.explanation_correct: DuckDuckGo is a search engine best known for its privacy-focused approach and minimal tracking. It became popular as an alternative to major ad-driven search services.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are search engines, but they are not known primarily for the same privacy-first model. They also have different ownership and feature sets.

questions.question: Which discussion website organizes its communities into “subreddits”?
questions.explanation_correct: Reddit users submit posts and comments within communities called subreddits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quora, Digg and Hacker News have different structures.

questions.question: Which instant messaging service was identified by a numeric user ID and became popular in the 1990s?
questions.explanation_correct: ICQ was an early internet messenger known for its numeric UIN identifiers and distinctive notification sound. It was one of the first widely adopted instant messaging services.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are instant messengers from similar eras, but they are not the service described here. Their naming and identification systems were different.

questions.question: Which file-sharing protocol popularized distributing file pieces among peers in a “swarm”?
questions.explanation_correct: BitTorrent distributes pieces of a file among peers in a swarm.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other peer-to-peer systems have their own designs; some also support segmented transfers.

questions.question: Which gaming webcomic was created by Scott Kurtz?
questions.explanation_correct: Scott Kurtz created the long-running webcomic PvP.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ctrl+Alt+Del was created by Tim Buckley; the other titles have different creators.

questions.question: Which 'Advice Animal' was the first to use the multi-colored wheel background and usually suggests destructive behaviors?
questions.explanation_correct: It paved the way for the entire 'Advice Animal' format of image macros.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Success Kid is about small victories; Bad Luck Brian is about misfortune.

questions.question: Which viral hit from 2007 features a deep-voiced singer moving away from the mic to breathe in between lyrics?
questions.explanation_correct: Tay Zonday's song became famous for its unique voice and social commentary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Numa Numa is a lip-sync video, and the others are reaction-based videos.

questions.question: Which forum software was developed by former vBulletin developers as a competing platform?
questions.explanation_correct: XenForo was developed by former vBulletin developers as separate forum software.
questions.explanation_incorrect: phpBB, Invision Power Board and Simple Machines Forum are other forum platforms.

questions.question: Which Adobe browser plugin powered many online games and animations before being discontinued?
questions.explanation_correct: Adobe Flash Player powered animations, games and other interactive content; Adobe discontinued it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Java, Silverlight and QuickTime were other technologies used for web content.

questions.question: Which internet slang expression is commonly used to indicate laughter?
questions.explanation_correct: LOL is an abbreviation for “laughing out loud,” a common internet shorthand for laughter. It became one of the most widely recognized early chat acronyms.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options mean different things: BRB means “be right back,” IMHO means “in my humble opinion,” and TTYL means “talk to you later.”

questions.question: Which Adobe technology powered many browser-based games and animations in the 2000s?
questions.explanation_correct: Flash was widely used for interactive animations and games on websites.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Animated GIFs, SVG and Java applets also supported web animation or interactivity, but were different technologies.

questions.question: Which Shiba Inu meme became known for colorful captions such as “much wow” and “such amaze”?
questions.explanation_correct: Doge became famous for captions written in playful, deliberately unconventional English.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cheems is another Shiba Inu meme; Grumpy Cat and Success Kid depict different subjects.

questions.question: Which online encyclopedia project, launched in 2001, is famously built and maintained by a community of volunteers?
questions.explanation_correct: Wikipedia is a free, multilingual, open-collaboration online encyclopedia launched in 2001.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Britannica, Encarta, and World Book are proprietary, expert-written commercial encyclopedias.

questions.question: What is the name of the phrase associated with the famous online raid incident shouting a player’s name?
questions.explanation_correct: Leeroy Jenkins is the catchphrase from a widely shared World of Warcraft video in which a player rushes in while shouting his name. The clip became an early internet viral sensation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options refer to different memes or viral phrases and are not the name tied to that specific raid-video catchphrase.

questions.question: Which early graphical web browser was developed at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications?
questions.explanation_correct: NCSA Mosaic was one of the first widely used graphical web browsers and was developed at NCSA. It helped popularize browsing the World Wide Web.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are later browsers or unrelated software, and they were not the specific early browser developed at NCSA.

questions.question: Which Google co-founder later became CEO of Alphabet in 2015 before stepping down from that role in 2019?
questions.explanation_correct: Larry Page co-founded Google with Sergey Brin and served as Alphabet CEO from 2015 to 2019.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sergey Brin was Google’s other co-founder; Steve Jobs and Jeff Bezos founded other companies.

questions.question: Which tech founder is associated with the creation of Facebook?
questions.explanation_correct: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook, one of the most influential social networking platforms. He became its best-known founder and CEO.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are founders of different online platforms or networks and are not the correct founder for Facebook.

questions.question: Which specific phrase, often paired with cats, became the hallmark of the 'Lolcat' image-macro trend?
questions.explanation_correct: The 'I Can Has Cheezburger' blog popularized the 'I Can Has' phrase as a staple of Lolcat memes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While these are all famous meme phrases, they originated from different internet subcultures or movies.

questions.question: Which singer is associated with the viral song 'Chocolate Rain'?
questions.explanation_correct: Tay Zonday is the singer who performed “Chocolate Rain,” a viral internet video and song from the late 2000s. The clip became a major meme of its era.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are performers linked to different viral songs or videos and are not the singer behind “Chocolate Rain.”

questions.question: Which person created the gaming webcomic Ctrl+Alt+Del?
questions.explanation_correct: Tim Buckley is the creator of the gaming webcomic Ctrl+Alt+Del. He is known for work centered on video game culture and internet comics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are authors or cartoonists associated with different works and genres. None of them created Ctrl+Alt+Del.

questions.question: Which company created the forum software vBulletin?
questions.explanation_correct: Jelsoft created vBulletin, a widely used internet forum software package. The company was later associated with the software's development history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are companies or groups tied to different forum platforms. They are not the original creator of vBulletin.

questions.question: Which Wikipedia co-founder also co-founded the for-profit web portal Wikia, later known as Fandom?
questions.explanation_correct: Jimmy Wales co-founded Wikipedia with Larry Sanger and later co-founded Wikia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Larry Sanger was also a Wikipedia co-founder, but was not a Wikia co-founder. Ward Cunningham and Brewster Kahle are associated with other projects.

questions.question: Which Microsoft service was its well-known instant messaging client?
questions.explanation_correct: MSN Messenger was Microsoft's instant messaging service. It was a major chat client before being rebranded and phased out.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices were messaging services from different companies. They were not Microsoft's client.

questions.question: Which peer-to-peer client is associated with the eDonkey network?
questions.explanation_correct: eMule is a peer-to-peer client designed for the eDonkey network. It became one of the best-known clients for that ecosystem.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are peer-to-peer applications or protocols tied to different networks. They are not the eDonkey client being asked about.

questions.question: Which animator created the web series Salad Fingers?
questions.explanation_correct: David Firth is the animator behind Salad Fingers. The series became an early cult favorite on the internet.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are animators or creators of other shows and films. They did not create Salad Fingers.

questions.question: What is a common name for alternating upper- and lowercase text used to imitate a mocking tone?
questions.explanation_correct: Mocking case is a name for alternating capitalization often paired with the mocking SpongeBob meme.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Leetspeak substitutes characters for letters; the other options are not the common name requested.

questions.question: Which YouTube co-founder uploaded the site’s first video, “Me at the zoo”?
questions.explanation_correct: Jawed Karim co-founded YouTube with Steve Chen and Chad Hurley and uploaded “Me at the zoo.”
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chen and Hurley were also YouTube co-founders; Bram Cohen is associated with BitTorrent.

questions.question: Which open-source web server, launched in the 1990s, became a major force in web hosting?
questions.explanation_correct: Apache HTTP Server was launched in 1995 and became one of the most widely used web servers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nginx, IIS and LiteSpeed are other web server products.

questions.question: Which reaction image uses Futurama's Fry with a doubtful caption style?
questions.explanation_correct: Not Sure Fry is the meme featuring Futurama's Fry with a skeptical expression. It is commonly used as a reaction image.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different reaction memes built around other subjects or expressions. They do not feature Fry in the same format.

questions.question: Which browser, released in 1994, later gained JavaScript, created by Netscape developer Brendan Eich?
questions.explanation_correct: Netscape Navigator was released in 1994; Eich created JavaScript at Netscape in 1995.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Internet Explorer, Mosaic and Opera were other browsers; Eich did not create Navigator itself.

questions.question: Which cat meme features a cat peering through a hole in a ceiling?
questions.explanation_correct: Ceiling Cat is an internet meme featuring a cat looking down through a ceiling opening.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Keyboard Cat, Longcat and Grumpy Cat are different cat memes.

questions.question: Which privacy-focused search engine is known for offering Google search results while protecting users’ privacy?
questions.explanation_correct: Startpage offers search results from Google with privacy protections.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other services use different arrangements for obtaining search results.

questions.question: Who created the office-themed comic strip Dilbert?
questions.explanation_correct: Scott Adams created Dilbert, an office-themed comic strip.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gary Larson, Bill Amend and Randall Munroe created other comics.

questions.question: Who filmed and narrated the viral “Double Rainbow” video?
questions.explanation_correct: Paul Vasquez filmed the video and became known for his excited reaction to a double rainbow.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other people are associated with different work or viral videos.

questions.question: Which social news website let users vote for a story by clicking “Digg”?
questions.explanation_correct: Digg used votes called diggs to surface submitted stories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Reddit, Slashdot and Delicious are different services.

questions.question: Which file-sharing application used the FastTrack peer-to-peer network?
questions.explanation_correct: Kazaa was a popular file-sharing client associated with the FastTrack network.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Napster, LimeWire and eMule were associated with other file-sharing systems.

questions.question: Which open-source forum project was originally known as MyBulletinBoard?
questions.explanation_correct: MyBB was originally known as MyBulletinBoard and is an open-source forum project.
questions.explanation_incorrect: phpBB and Discourse are also open source, but are different projects; vBulletin is a separate product.

questions.question: Which image macro depicts a thoughtful velociraptor asking philosophical questions?
questions.explanation_correct: Philosoraptor is an image macro of a pondering raptor paired with philosophical questions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Advice Dog, Bad Luck Brian and Success Kid depict different meme characters.

questions.question: Which animator created the Brackenwood series featuring Bitey?
questions.explanation_correct: Adam Phillips is the animator behind Brackenwood and its character Bitey.
questions.explanation_incorrect: David Firth created Salad Fingers; the other animators are associated with different work.
